title: The New Fan’s Guide to the Unreal World of Nathan Fielder
gist: A fan's guide to Nathan Fielder's style ahead of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything, arguing his persona-driven, simulation-heavy method is well suited to probing Holmes and the Theranos-era tech industry's blurring of reality.

insights.claim: Nathan Fielder codirected with Lance Oppenheim the three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything, after the pair lived with Holmes and her partner Billy Evans in Del Mar, California, for over a month in 2023 until she reported to prison for an 11-year sentence.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: A high-profile cultural retelling of the Theranos fraud is coming to cinemas.

insights.claim: Theranos reached a peak valuation of $9 billion in 2014 before its blood test machine was revealed to be vaporware, and Holmes styled herself as the next Steve Jobs to hype a bogus advance in medical science.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Canonical example of narrative-driven founder fraud in venture investing.
insights.locator: There has been no shortage of coverage

insights.claim: Film scholar Kate Rennebohm sees Holmes as an avatar of a tech industry with ambitions of exceeding or dispensing human reality itself, making the Fielder-Holmes meeting an unstoppable-force-meets-immovable-object collision.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Frames founder-myth culture as a recurring Silicon Valley risk factor.
insights.locator: Rennebohm says that Holmes also serves as an avatar

insights.claim: Fielder's work centers on constructed personas and elaborate simulations (Nathan for You, The Rehearsal), and academic Andrew Bricker argues the paradox is that his revelations of truth arrive only through that artificial framework.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Explains why the documentary may blur fact and fiction rather than deliver a conventional exposé.
insights.locator: Bricker points out that the fundamental “paradox”

insights.claim: Fielder's tactics include deadpan silence and flat echoing of subjects' words, which Bricker says often lead subjects to blurt out surprising confessions.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Suggests the film may elicit unguarded admissions from Holmes.

insights.claim: Critics split on whether Fielder exploits ordinary people drawn into his plots or simply reflects a dysfunctional society back at us, making his shows litmus tests on empathy.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Reception of the film will hinge on this ethical divide.
insights.locator: But while Holmes may be deserving of invasive scrutiny
